chunks: And he entered his garden, while he was unjust to himself, saying: 'I do not think that this will ever perish.'

key_terms.جَنَّتَهُ: his garden (often symbolizing wealth and prosperity)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'while he was unjust to himself' signify in the context of the garden owner?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is frequently linked to Qarun (Korah) or the wealthy companion of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in Surah Al-Kahf, illustrating the spiritual peril of *ghurur* (self-deception) where material abundance blinds one to divine power. The declaration 'I do not think this will ever perish' highlights the arrogance of attributing permanence to transient worldly creations, a theme central to the Surah's narrative of contrasting faith and wealth.
